findings.title: A card that hid a masked killer's name as '?' gives the name in clear when its words are served or rewritten after the mask has ended
findings.where: scripts/secret.mjs:496-499 (wordsFor reads the mask as it stands now), 1207-1211 and 1235-1239 (the posting GM keeps its own words, cut for a GM: unmasked), 958-991 (answerWordsRequest cuts the held words for the asker at the time of the ask), 1343-1365 (updateSecret cuts at the time of the rewrite); scripts/mask-gm.mjs:135-137 (namesHiddenFrom answers [] for a GM) and the header's WHEN IT ENDS (a new time of day ends the mask, no reveal needed)
findings.what_happens: The mask (owner-115 item 1b) is applied once, as each copy of a card's words is cut for its reader. The posting GM's own copy is cut for a GM, which hides nothing, so the GM's store holds the masked character's real name (its `html`, and `lines` where the card has you/them lines). When a reader who missed the card - offline when it was posted, or on another device - returns, `answerWordsRequest` cuts those held words with `wordsFor(sender.id, words)`, which asks `nameMask(userId)` now. Once the time of day that the mask lived in is over, `namesHiddenFrom` answers no names, so the returning reader is sent the killer's name where the card everyone else read said '?'. The same holds for `updateSecret` after the mask ends: a ruling settled (call-gm.mjs `settleCall`) or a Reroll's mark (reroll.mjs:763-770, inside the 30-minute Reroll window) re-sends the GM's unmasked words, cut with the mask of that moment, to every reader.
findings.failure_scenario: During a masked murder the killer Steals from a bystander whose connection has dropped; the next time of day ends the mask without a reveal; the bystander reconnects, their browser asks the GM for the card's words, and the card reads 'Kaito takes ...' where every connected reader of that moment read '? takes ...'.
findings.expected: A card's words keep the mask they were posted under for every reader outside it: the cut made at posting time is the one a returning reader and a rewrite get (for example, the names hidden at posting kept with the entry and applied again at answer and at updateSecret).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a mask kept with the entry: `remember` stores html, summary, meta, readers, lines, world, authorHold, pin, trusted (secret.mjs:793-807), nothing of the mask. Looked for a check in answerWordsRequest (958-991) and in onSecretPacket's GM branch (1497-1509): none. namesHiddenFrom reads masked tokens on every scene now (mask-gm.mjs:139-144), and the mask's restorePatch takes the token flag off at the end, so after the end it answers []. R7403 (tests-tier1.mjs:59187-59204) drives wordsFor with a stand-in mask at one moment only; tier 2's catch-up tests (tests-tier2.mjs:39720-39744, 40721-40763) were not read to hold a mask. No test found that ends a mask between a post and a return. Not run.
findings.tests_near: R7403 (tier 1); scenario 21 'outside the fight' (named in secret.mjs:454-457); tier 2 'a returning reader is given the line written for them' (named in secret.mjs:392-393). None read to cross a mask's end.

findings.title: The freed victim's 'You can act again' line is never served after a return: the author GM's held copy keeps the other readers and the other line
findings.where: scripts/murder-rules.mjs:3691-3708 (tellIncidentClosed posts to the other participants, then updateSecret to the freed victim); scripts/secret.mjs:1235-1243 (the author GM keeps the words with readers = the first whisper list, authorHold), 1350-1357 (updateSecret remembers only on a browser that is a reader), 970-977 (the asker must be among the held readers)
findings.what_happens: tellIncidentClosed is posted by a GM to players alone (incidentAudienceIds holds no GM), so the GM keeps the words as an author's hold with readers = `others` and html = DRPG.Murder.closedYou. The victim's line is then sent with updateSecret(message, closedVictimYou, freed). The GM is not in `freed`, so `remember` is not called on it: its hold keeps readers `others` and the others' words. A freed victim who was not connected at the close asks the GMs at their return; answerWordsRequest finds their id not among the readers and sends nothing, and the card is drawn with DRPG.Secret.wordsElsewhere. The comment on heldReadersAfter (secret.mjs:838-841) names exactly this line as the case it serves.
findings.failure_scenario: A direct murder closes with its victim alive while the victim's player is disconnected; when they reconnect, the card in their chat says 'A private card. Its words did not reach this browser.' instead of 'The incident is over. You can act again.', and nothing else tells them they may act.
findings.expected: The author GM's hold follows updateSecret: the new readers are added and the words they are to be given kept for them (heldReadersAfter's own rule).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether any GM is a reader of this card: incidentAudienceIds returns the owners of seats' characters only ('GMs are not in it', incident-store.mjs:392-394); announce routes a whisper list to postSecret, and murder-rules.mjs:110-111 veils it, so the document names everybody and readersOf on another GM answers [] (secret.mjs:1378-1383). Checked whether the freed victim could be in `others`: the two lists are disjoint (murder-rules.mjs:3697-3698). A freed victim connected at the close gets the words by the socket and keeps them across a reload (the store is a client setting), so only a missed card is affected. Not run.

findings.title: The season reset's 'each to their own bedroom' pans only the last bedroom's players: SYNC.gather packets of one burst are merged, newest tokenIds winning
findings.where: scripts/season-wipe.mjs:574-578 (one broadcast(SYNC.gather) per bedroom batch, after each teleport); scripts/sync.mjs:255-279 (the coalescer merges a burst's data field by field, newest winning), 530 (the gather row runs `camera` once with that data); scripts/call-world.mjs:684-694 (panToGathered pans only to this client's token among `tokenIds`)
findings.what_happens: The bus merges every event of a kind that arrives within `coalesceMs` (120 ms) of the last, up to 360 ms, into one run whose data is the merge of the burst, each field the newest push's (sync.mjs:224-233, 265). That is right for a state and wrong for an event: placeCast sends one gather per bedroom - `{ room, scene, tokenIds }` of that bedroom's tokens - so when two teleports finish inside 120 ms the earlier packet's `tokenIds` is replaced by the later one's, on every browser and on the GM's own (`broadcast` applies locally too). Each player's browser pans only if its own token is in the merged `tokenIds`, so the players of the earlier bedrooms in the burst are not panned to where their token now stands.
findings.failure_scenario: The GM resets a season with the cast sent each to their own bedroom; the tokens move, but on most players' screens the camera stays on the room they were in, and only the players of the last one or two bedrooms are panned to their token.
findings.expected: Every gather is a camera event of its own: either the bus does not merge `gather` (its row is an event, not a state), or placeCast sends one packet with every batch's tokens.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a gather that is not merged: `apply` is the one coalescer for every kind (sync.mjs:279) and the socket handler calls it (157). Looked for another camera road after the reset: placeCast hands `teleportTokens` pan: false (call-world.mjs:556), as the gather does. Tests read the packets emitted (tests-tier2.mjs:61879, 64308) and tier 0 reads the order of teleport and broadcast (tests-tier0.mjs:14094-14095); none reads the pans of several batches. gatherEveryone and returnTheLiving send one packet each, so only placeCast is affected. Whether two teleports finish inside 120 ms on a real server is not measured (not_established).

findings.what_happens: A stash's concealment is the one fact Find Stash (Analyze, Head 16) exists to open, and it is written on the room's region documents, which Foundry sends to every browser with the scene. A player's console reads every region's `drpgStashes` and learns which rooms hold a hidden stash and whose it is; the owner's actor id there names the student. The opening itself is still the GM's (stash-reach.mjs:472 asks the GMs' found notes), so what goes is the location, not the contents' reach.

findings.expected: Either a hidden stash's place lives where only the GMs and its owner read it (the GM store, as `found` became a GM flag at E16), or the trade is written down as a decision beside WORLD_SECRET_RULES with its reason.
findings.refutation_tried: Searched scripts/world-secrets.mjs for Region, stash and drpgStashes: no rule. Searched scripts/gm-stores.mjs: the stash rows are the rifles' (951-965), not the concealment. Searched docs/handbooks for a statement that the place of a hidden stash is public: the GM handbook (gm-handbook.en.md:923) says a hidden stash 'is found only with Analyze > Find Stash'. The code comment at 1576-1582 calls it a known leak, but it predates the trust model D2 and the E04/E05 rules, and no stage paper found records the owner's choice. That a player's browser holds the scene's regions is Foundry's rule, not read on v14 for regions specifically.

findings.title: The GM who wrote a card to players alone is told on that card 'Its words did not reach this browser', which holds them
findings.where: scripts/secret.mjs:657-660 (secretHtml answers null for an author's hold), 1026-1036 and 909-927 (a wordless card is drawn with elsewhereHtml after 4 s); lang/en.json:6082, lang/pl.json:6531
findings.what_happens: Since E38 the author GM keeps the words of a card it whispered to players alone (a tail, a door, a Reroll receipt, an incident's close) and does not read them itself, by the owner's choice (docs/dev/e38/STATUS.md:31-40). The card is still in that GM's chat log (its author sees it), so drawPrivateCard finds no words, gives the card its 4-second wait and then draws DRPG.Secret.wordsElsewhere, 'A private card. Its words did not reach this browser.' The sentence is false on that browser and reads like a failed delivery; the comment at 658-659 and E38's STATUS say the author 'sees its stub'.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM whispers a Reroll receipt to a player and four seconds later reads on their own card that its words did not reach this browser, and asks the player whether the card arrived.
findings.expected: An author's held card is drawn with a line of its own (for example 'A private card to its readers.'), or with the stub the comment and E38's paper describe.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether the author GM's log draws the card at all: Foundry shows a whispered message to its author; E58's reading (LOCAL-REPORT.md item S7-4) records that every message reaches every browser. Checked whether wordless() spares an authorHold entry: it asks secretHtml(message) === null (secret.mjs:900-901), which an authorHold answers. That the author does not read the words is a recorded decision (by_decision); only the sentence is the finding. Scenario 98 B2 reads 'the author GM a dash' (E38 STATUS:33) - isStub stays true for elsewhereHtml (secret.mjs:124-131), so it would not tell the two apart.

findings.title: A returning player asks for every veiled card's words, and the newest veiled cards that are not theirs take the eight notice slots
findings.where: scripts/secret.mjs:935-951 (askForWords: `mine` is every wordless card whose whisper list names this user), 1194 (a veiled card's whisper list is the whole table), 943-944 (the newest RETURN_NOTICES of `mine` raise a notice)

findings.expected: The notice slots go to the cards answered (the first answer of each), or the ask leaves out veiled cards whose meta this browser cannot tie to itself.

findings.title: `gmAsk` raises a popup on every GM's screen and is not among the flags a player's card may not carry
findings.where: scripts/secret.mjs:224 (gmAsk is a placement flag, kept on an ordinary thread card's document), 247 (GM_META: gmPopup, popupForce ... not gmAsk), 1314-1315 (postAsked keeps it for the sender's own thread), 1487-1488 (a player's meta keeps it); scripts/messenger-app.mjs:547-560 (a GM's browser raises a popup for any thread card carrying gmAsk, deliberately not by author); scripts/private-rolls.mjs:1265 (GM_ONLY_FLAGS has no gmAsk)
findings.what_happens: GM_META's rule is that 'a card that interrupts the GMs (gmPopup, popupForce) ... is the module's to post, not a console's'. gmAsk does the same on a GM's browser - a popup titled DRPG.Messenger.gmActionTitle with the card's words - and messenger.mjs:362 says a player's own messenger card carries none. A player's console can post a card in their own thread with gmAsk (on the document, or in the meta of a veiled card, or through card.post), and every GM's screen raises the popup; sheet-audit's 'forged' row does not name it either.
findings.failure_scenario: A player sends a stream of their own thread cards marked gmAsk from the console, and each GM's screen raises a 'GM action' popup for each one while the GM runs a scene.
findings.expected: gmAsk on a player's card is treated as gmPopup is: dropped from a player's meta and postAsked's flags, and named by the forged-flag row when it is on a player's document.
findings.refutation_tried: Read messenger-app.mjs:538-560: the GM branch asks only the flag and wordsOf, not the writer. Read threadStatsOf (messenger.mjs:146-149): gmAsk also counts a GM's own card as unread, which a player's card already is. A player could write any flag on its own document anyway, so the meta filter alone cannot close it; the forged-flag list would. Severity nit: a nuisance, no rule or secret moves. Not run.

by_decision.what: The relay passes a player's change to any actor that is not a student (an adversary, a companion) between 0 and its maximum, Fear one step at a time without a limit, an item's charges with no upper bound.
The author GM of a card to players alone keeps its words for the readers' return and does not read them itself.
No server-side copy of a private card's words: a GM or player whose card's GMs were all away waits.
A returning reader's ask is judged on Foundry's sender id, not bridge-guards.mjs senderOf (which also wants the user connected as the GM sees it).
An ordinary thread card keeps its placement flags (thread, kind, gmAsk) on its document; a veiled card carries them in its meta.
A non-recipient still reads that a private card exists, when, and by whom (the author is Foundry's server stamp); while an incident runs or a mask stands the GM posts a player's private cards.
Only the newest eight cards of a return raise a notice.
by_decision.source: scripts/secret.mjs:878-881 ('a choice of this commit's, not a measurement')

by_decision.what: The account match's record is a world setting, not a GM store, and keeps a season, not a student.
The relay guard drops Daggerheart's packets on every GM but the primary (one writer).
iso-shield leaves scene configuration and the canvas to the isometric module.
A locked room counts in the room census; a lock is announced only when it opens.
A Search reaches into no stash; a hidden stash opens to Find Stash alone.

hygiene.functions_note: Measured by a line script over top-level functions and object literals: the longest function is secret.mjs `post` (1163-1246, 84 lines); the longest literals are vault-store.mjs VAULT_FLAGS (90-193, 104 lines, mostly comment) and sync.mjs REFRESHES (367-452, 86).
duplicated_helpers: A key's description markup is built three times and compared as a string: grantKeyNow (vault-store.mjs:326-329), repointDeadKey's `text` (368-369) and keyCopiesAfterOwnerLeft's `text` (531-532); the two comparisons (370, 386, 542) hold only while the three stay byte for byte the same (see not_established on the stored HTML).
secret.mjs `hasLines` (398-401) and the same test inline in cutWords (503).
Cut at 160 with an ellipsis twice in relay-guard.mjs: plainWhat (1101-1102, a literal 160) and studentTrace (568, TRACE_VALUE).
dead_code: vault-store.mjs `bedroomKeyKey` (289) and `takeOldOwnersKeys` (491): re-exported by vault.mjs (28-29), imported by no file of scripts/ or audit/harness through it (git grep -w); used inside vault-store.mjs only. Kept by the facade rule (vault.mjs keeps every name it exported).
vault-store.mjs `isConcealed` (1124) and `vaultRoomFor` (1138): reached from api.mjs (game.drpg) alone, as their notes say.

refresh: sync.mjs merges every kind's burst field by field (255-279): a kind whose data is an event and not a state loses all but the newest packet's data inside 120 ms. Today only SYNC.gather carries such data (finding 3); a refresh pass adding a kind with data should know it.
The private-card swap is registered at ready (module.mjs:454): whether v14 draws the chat log's first batch before that hook exists is not read (not_established).

not_established.what: Whether two bedroom teleports of placeCast finish within 120 ms of each other on a real server (finding 3's precondition).
not_established.why: The harness has no Region#teleportTokens and takes the fallback (call-world.mjs:542-549); timing on a real server is not in any recorded reading.

l1.what: The gap between placeCast's gather packets
recipe: On the GM's page, before a season reset to bedrooms, wrap game.socket.emit to log Date.now() for each packet with action 'sync' and kind 'gather'.
Reset the season with 'each to their own bedroom' for at least four students.
Read the gaps between the logged packets.
l1.settles_if: finding 3 holds at that table if any gap is under 120 ms; it is latent there if every gap is over 360 ms

not_established.what: Whether v14 stores a granted key's `system.description` byte for byte, so that repointDeadKey's and keyCopiesAfterOwnerLeft's string comparisons (vault-store.mjs:370, 386, 542) match a room or owner name with an apostrophe or an ampersand.
not_established.why: secret.mjs:136-142 records that Foundry normalised a chat message's HTML on its round trip; an Item description's round trip on v14 is not read, and escapeHTML writes entities for ' and &.

l1.what: A key's stored description against the grant's text
recipe: GM gives a bedroom named Kaede's Room to a student whose name has no apostrophe (the grant makes a key).

On the GM's console: compare the key's system.description with `

${game.i18n.format('DRPG.Vault.keyDescription', { room: foundry.utils.escapeHTML("Kaede's Room"), owner: foundry.utils.escapeHTML(actor.name) })}

`.
l1.settles_if: the comparisons hold if the two strings are equal; if not, a rename the carry missed makes a second key and a room given away leaves the new owner's key text unrewritten

not_established.what: Whether v14 draws the chat log's first cards before the ready hook that registers the private-card swap (module.mjs:454, secret.mjs:1524-1530), which would show a dash on cards this browser holds words for, and a stub instead of a hidden card for others' veiled cards, until each is redrawn.
not_established.why: Foundry's order of the sidebar's first render against `ready` is not in the repository; the module's note (module.mjs:451-453) addresses a card arriving before, not cards drawn before.

l1.what: Private cards in the chat log right after a load
recipe: As a player who holds the words of several private cards and of none of an incident's veiled cards to others, reload the page.
Before scrolling or anything else redraws, read the chat log's cards.
l1.settles_if: settled as no defect if every held card shows its words and no veiled card of others is drawn; a defect if dashes or stubs show
